diagnosis: I calibrated HBV on daily NSE over 1971-10 to 1997-12 using the global DDS optimiser, run twice from different starting points and seeds. Both runs reached the same ceiling: NSE 0.646 and 0.648, KGE about 0.77, r 0.81. The run I submit has a bias of -3%, so the water balance is about right. Fit is only moderate for an upland catchment. The likely reason is that a single lumped snow routine with one temperature series cannot represent snow across 70–1309 m. The optimiser compensates with a high snow threshold (TT about 1.2 °C), reduced snowfall (SFCF about 0.73), fast melt (CFMAX about 5.6) and almost no refreezing or retained meltwater (CFR and CWH at their lower bounds). Spring melt timing and rain-on-snow peaks are probably the weakest periods, along with the very large flood peaks. Simulated maximum flow is about 24 mm/d against 33 mm/d observed. Confidence: the snow and water-balance parameters (TT, CFMAX, SFCF, PERC about 4.5, K2 about 0.05) came out almost the same in both runs. The fast-response and soil parameters (K0, UZL, LP, BETA, FC from 145 to 190 mm) differ a lot between equally good runs. Both runs pinned some parameters to their range limits, and I did not widen those ranges and recalibrate. I also did no split-sample check, so the expected NSE in 1998–2008 is roughly 0.6–0.65, untested.
